senses.gloss:
Nai-dāgha is the name of the ‘summer’ season in the later Saṃhitās and Brāhmaṇas. Cf. ṛtu and nidāgha.
Foot notes Av. ix. 5, 31; taittirīya brāhmaṇa, i. 8, 4, 2; Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, i. 4, 1, 16, etc.; naidāghīya, ‘belonging to the summer,’ pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa, xxiii. 16, 8, etc.

Nai-dāna is a term applied in the nirukta to a class of Vedic interpreters. Roth takes the Naidānas to be ‘etymologists,’ but Sieg thinks they are the same as the Aitihāsikas or ‘legendarists.’
Foot notes vi. 9; vii. 12.
St. Petersburg Dictionary, s.v. But of. nirukta, Erlāuterungen, 220, 221; Muir, Sanskrit Texts, 2^2, 176.
Die Sagenstoffe des ṛgveda, 29.
The word seems to mean ‘one concerned with the original form’ (nidāna).

Nai-dhruvi, ‘descendant of Nidhruva,’ is the patronymic of kaśyapa in the Bṛhadāraṇyaka upaniṣad.
Foot notes vi. 4, 33 (Mādhyandina = vi. 5, 3 kāṇva).
Nai-ṣāda, a ‘man of niṣāda,’ is mentioned in the kauṣītaki brāhmaṇa (xxv. 15) and the Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā (xxx. 8).
